sentenceSets.sentence: She prepared a précis of the report for those who needed the conclusions without the methodology.

answerChoices.reasoning: An abstract is written by the author and published with the work itself, but she prepared this separately afterward for a particular group of readers.
An outline lays out the skeleton of a document's organization, whereas these readers want the conclusions delivered, not a map of where the report puts things.
An excerpt lifts passages unchanged from the original, but omitting the methodology while keeping the conclusions requires condensing the whole rather than quoting a part.
A digest gathers and organizes material from many sources, while she worked from a single report.
An appendix adds supporting material at the end, which is the opposite of stripping the methodology away.
A transcript reproduces spoken words in full and would preserve everything rather than cutting the methodology.
An affidavit is a sworn written statement and has no place in circulating a report's findings internally.
Annotations are notes added alongside a text, but these readers are being spared the text rather than given commentary on it.
Enlarging the report would defeat the purpose of serving readers who want less of it.
A rebuttal argues against the report, whereas she is passing its conclusions along.
A bill for payment is unrelated to conveying a report's findings.

sentenceSets.sentence: Each cadet was required to reduce the forty-page field manual to a one-page precis that a squad leader could read in the dark.

answerChoices.reasoning: A synopsis conventionally summarizes the plot of a narrative work, but this exercise condenses an instructional manual down to what a squad leader must know to act.
A checklist is a bare series of items to tick off, whereas the assignment is to reduce the manual itself, preserving its substance in shorter form.
A paraphrase restates a text in different words at roughly the same length, which cannot take forty pages down to one.
An index points to where topics appear in the original, but a squad leader reading in the dark has no manual to turn to.
A facsimile reproduces the original exactly and would still run to forty pages.
Errata list corrections to a printed text rather than compress its contents.
A glossary defines terms and would leave the manual's actual instructions out.
A manifest inventories cargo or passengers, which has nothing to do with condensing a field manual.
An anthology collects many works together, the opposite of reducing one to a page.
Elaborating adds detail, which would take the manual past forty pages rather than down to one.
A weapon is not something a cadet writes on a single page.

sentenceSets.sentence: The minister read only the precis her staff had left on the desk, which is why she was unprepared for the question about the Kenyan supplier.

answerChoices.reasoning: A briefing is an oral session in which aides walk an official through a matter, but this was left on the desk as a document to be read.
A memorandum conveys new information or instruction of its own, whereas the failure here is that a longer source existed and she took only its shortened version.
A dossier is a thick collection of documents on a subject, which would have contained the detail about the supplier rather than omitting it.
A transcript records everything said and could not have left out the Kenyan supplier.
An agenda lists the items to be taken up, but her gap was in substance rather than in knowing what topics would arise.
A communiqué is an official statement issued outward to the public, not a document left for a minister's own preparation.
A subpoena compels testimony and is not reading material prepared by staff.
An itinerary sets out travel arrangements and would not bear on a question about a supplier.
'Verbatim' describes reproducing every word, which would have included the detail she lacked.
Applause is not something left on a desk to be read.
A water jug is an object on a desk, not something one reads before a hearing.
